# simplicio-loop — LLM quick orientation

Start here, in order:
1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `docs/LLM_MAX_SPEED_ORIENTATION.md`  # always-on max-speed law for every host LLM
3. `.claude/skills/simplicio-loop/SKILL.md`  # includes SIMPLICIO-LLM-ORIENTATION re-feed block
4. `README.md`

What this repo is:
- Runtime-agnostic autonomous looping orchestrator (`/simplicio-loop`)
- Current reference task flow for the Simplicio line
- Evidence-gated loop: never exit on a fake “done”
- Runs on 35 agent hosts. `simplicio_loop/_catalog/harnesses.json` lists them; install a `wired` one with `scripts/install.sh <runtime>`; per-host notes are in `adapters/<host>/README.md`.

Current operator flow:
- `simplicio-loop "<task>" [--verify "<tests>"]` (short for `simplicio-loop turbo --repo . --task "<task>"`) — the default way to run any task, no provider and no API key, ONE command. When the host has a headless CLI ([docs/HARNESSES.md](docs/HARNESSES.md)) it runs Mapper, the model through that CLI (same model, account and configuration), dev-cli edits and `--verify`, and prints the result (`mode: "hybrid"`): `status` ok or failed is final, report it as printed. Only when it prints a `needs_plan` request (with `reason: "hybrid_unavailable: <cause>"`) you are the model: run the printed `apply` command once with your JSON plan as its heredoc body (`simplicio-loop turbo --repo . --apply - --verify "<tests>" <<'PLAN'`, the plan, `PLAN`; `simplicio-dev-cli` applies it and runs `--verify`), and on `failed` fix the plan once and run it again. Do not explore, list or read files, and do not run the tests yourself. Never edit files by hand. Allow the one command once so the host never prompts: OpenCode `permission.bash` rule `"simplicio-loop *": "allow"` in `opencode.json`; Claude Code `Bash(simplicio-loop:*)` in the allow list (everything the engine runs inside that command is covered by that one approval).
- `simplicio-mapper --help` — survey operator; turbo runs it for you.
- `simplicio-dev-cli --help` — governed edit/verify operator; turbo drives it.
- Both operators are built into the one `simplicio-loop` wheel (`pip install simplicio-loop`); update with `simplicio-loop update`.
- Run focused tests and `git diff --check`; re-query live PR/check/merge state before publishing.
- `SIMPLICIO_EXECUTION_PROFILE=standalone` is the only execution profile; there is no Runtime/MCP backend in this stack.
- The survey every flow requires is Mapper-only.

Non-negotiables:
- Run commands for real; never simulate output.
- Never mark work done without green gates + evidence.
- Verify claims locally before push with `python3 scripts/check.py`.
- Keep `_bundle` and source in parity; `scripts/check.py` audits this.
- Do not use `simplicio-runtime`, `simplicio`, or Runtime MCP; record missing-operator residuals honestly.

Key loop artifacts:
- `.simplicio-loop/orchestrator/loop/scratchpad.md` — single source of truth for loop state
- `.simplicio-loop/orchestrator/loop/journal.jsonl` — durable attempt memory / stall detector input
- `.simplicio-loop/orchestrator/loop/phase.json` — current HRM phase
- `.simplicio-loop/orchestrator/loop/HANDOFF.md` — resume note for the next agent/runtime
- `.simplicio-loop/orchestrator/wiki/SUMMARY.md` — cross-agent persistent summary

Key commands:
- `python3 scripts/check.py`
- `python3 scripts/loop_journal.py resume`
- `python3 scripts/cross_agent_wiki.py summary`
- `python3 scripts/hierarchical_planner.py status`

Complete command/feature map: `docs/CLI_COMMANDS.md`. Before using any
entrypoint, run its most specific `--help`; public commands must explain their
purpose there. Current release: Loop 3.47.0 (Mapper 0.26.34 and Dev CLI
0.18.16 are bundled). Issue work uses objective, implementation/deployment, and
tests; do not add Acceptance Criteria sections.

If you are an LLM agent:
- Prefer deterministic edits / local verification.
- Do not use stale Mapper artifacts or fabricate a handoff; start a fresh bounded survey.
- Read the journal before retrying a failed approach.
- Treat blocker receipts and next-action hints in the wiki/handoff as first-class context.

<!-- simplicio-global-llm-architecture-rules:start -->
GLOBAL ARCHITECTURE RULES FOR LLMS

1. Do not preserve backward compatibility. Delete obsolete behavior directly;
   do not add compatibility layers, migrations, or fallbacks.
2. Choose the simplest implementation that meets the current need.
3. Build long-lived layers incrementally: make the minimum end-to-end version
   work first, then add capabilities without dismantling working code.
4. Keep components modular with clear separation of responsibilities.
5. Prefer mature, maintained libraries; do not rewrite from scratch without an
   explicit technical reason.
6. Inspect existing dependencies before adding packages or reimplementing.
7. Make architecture decisions for the long term; do not leave temporary
   solutions to change later.
8. Reuse validated patterns from mature products instead of reinventing them.

<!-- simplicio-global-llm-architecture-rules:end -->
